title: Rim shot synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic rim shot sample (v0.1, proposal, #296). Mono. Only schema_version and seed are required; an omitted field takes the default named in its description. Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. Voice: two damped sine partials (lower at f1_hz, upper at f1_hz * f2_ratio, level2 relative to the lower, each with its own exponential decay), high-passed at hp_hz, plus an optional short high-passed noise click. Time t is measured from the first sample of the sound (sample n_off with offset_ms). All numeric ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS from docs/research/2026-11-02_rim-targets.md section 5 and section 2 (hypotheses; the few sourced points are weak: one hobby page for 455 / 1667 Hz, nothing for level, decay, high-pass or click); they are placeholders until the audio-engineer measures them and the user listens. The audio-engineer may adjust them in the engine PR (a contract-change then). Not part of v0.1: a third partial (`f3_ratio`, only a low-confidence vendor listing), pitch `bend` (no source for the rim), a separate `clave` model (clave is the special case level2 0 with f1_hz near 2500), `tone_peak_*`, a note-name resolver for `f1_hz`.
$comment: Contract rules that JSON Schema cannot express or that are not field ranges. (1) Cross-field rule: hp_hz must be less than 0.8 * f1_hz (the high-pass must not eat the lower partial). The schema cannot compare two fields, so the engine rejects a violation with an error text (never clamps) and tests check it. An omitted partner: with the default hp_hz (200) every f1_hz in range (minimum 300, 0.8 * 300 = 240) satisfies the rule; with the default f1_hz (455) an explicit hp_hz of 364 or more violates it and is rejected by the engine. (2) Single partial: level2 0 means no upper partial (f2_ratio then has no effect); this is the only way to express it, there is no 'off' value in f2_ratio. (3) Highest partial: f1_hz * f2_ratio is at most 3500 * 5.0 = 17500 Hz, below 0.45 * sample_rate (19845 Hz at 44100), so no aliasing cross-field rule is needed; the click is band-limited below 0.45 * sample_rate by the engine. (4) Decay: decay1_ms and decay2_ms are the time from the end of the attack until that partial's envelope has fallen 60 dB (time to -60 dB after the attack), exponential, same definition as kick amp_decay_ms and hat decay_ms. A measured -60 dB time of the whole file can be None when the fade-out guard is reached first; -20 / -40 dB times are the comparison basis. (5) level2 is the amplitude of the upper partial relative to the lower one at t = 0 (linear, 1 = equal amplitude), before the high-pass. The two partials start with phase 0 (sine), fixed by this contract. (6) Click: click_level 0 means no click. The click is white noise high-passed at 4 kHz, with an exponential decay of click_ms (time to -60 dB), scaled by click_level relative to the lower partial's amplitude at t = 0; it takes its own sub-stream of the seed. (7) Determinism: the partials have no randomness; the seed changes only the click, so at click_level 0 the output is seed-independent. (8) Reject out-of-range values, never clamp. Defaults are placeholders until measured. (9) The file ends with a 5 ms linear fade-out like the kick, the first sample is 0, DC is removed as in clap. length_ms: a given length_ms shorter than the sound cuts it with the fade; if omitted the engine uses 200 ms and records it in the sidecar. Shared field names keep the meaning of clap-params and kick-params (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, drive, polarity, offset_ms, peak_ceiling_dbfs, preset); length_ms has its own range here. Engine identity for sidecars: engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-rim' with the rim engine's own version (sample-metadata.schema.json, D-025).

seed.description: Seeds the click (own sub-stream). The partials are deterministic. Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV.

length_ms.description: File length. If shorter than the sound needs, it is cut off and gets a 5 ms fade-out.

f1_hz.description: Frequency of the lower partial, Hz. Wide enough to include the clave case (about 2500 Hz).

f2_ratio.description: Upper partial frequency = f1_hz * f2_ratio. No effect at level2 0.

level2.description: Amplitude of the upper partial relative to the lower. 0 = single partial.

decay1_ms.description: Time to fall 60 dB after the attack for the lower partial, exponential.

decay2_ms.description: Time to fall 60 dB after the attack for the upper partial, exponential.

hp_hz.description: Corner of the high-pass, Hz. Must be less than 0.8 * f1_hz (cross-field rule, checked by the engine).

click_level.description: Level of the noise click relative to the lower partial. 0 = off (then the output is seed-independent).

click_ms.description: Time of the click to fall 60 dB, ms. No effect at click_level 0.

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation, same stage as kick drive. 0 = off.

polarity.description: Sign of the whole output, applied after the peak ceiling.

offset_ms.description: Silence before the sound, rounded to whole samples (as in kick-params).

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Peak ceiling of the quantised file.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.
